newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Trust Feeds killer Brian Mitchell on Tuesday became the first security force operative to receive amnesty from the truth commission in a decision announced five days before the amnesty application cut-off date.

- The Motion Picture Association, Hollywood's powerful lobbying arm, has complained to the office of the U.S. trade representative that South African authorites are not doing enough to crack down on video piracy.

- Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and its associates planned to spend a massive 30 billion rand in South Africa until 2001 on capital projects to improve competitivness and boost exports, deputy chairman Nicky Oppenheimer said on Tuesday.
- President Nelson Mandela danced with joy after signing the South African constitution into law on Tuesday.
- Natal Portland Cement's new 780 million rand cement factory hangs in the balance because of the slow growth of the cement market, the company said on Tuesday.

- Engen Ltd, buoyed by its strategic parntership with Malaysian-based Petronas, appears to be on track for further profit growth in the financial year to August 31 next year, Bernard Smith, the chairman said at the company's annual meeting on Tuesday.
- Pick 'n Pay Ltd has slammed the retention of legislation restricting the sale of liquor on Sundays, saying it was laughable because of a growing and increasingly demanding tourism industry.
- An elated President Mandela on Tuesday signed into law the new constitution, ushering in a new period of constitutional democracy and finally consigning apartheid to the dustbin of history.

- Former policeman Brian Mitchell, granted amnesty on Tuesday for his role in the massacre of 11 people at the rural settlement of Trust Feed, plans to become "constructively involved" with the Trust Feed community.
